(1) language meaning is grounded in human cognition, (2) human cognition includes probabilistic concepts, (3) probabilistic concepts can be used to model language meaning, (4) the resulting probabilistic models of language meaning can be used to predict and explain human behavior, and (5) probabilistic models of meaning are useful for understanding language use in context.

(1) probabilistic models of semantics and pragm- atics can provide a formal basis for understanding language meaning; and (2) the conceptual lexicon provides a unified framework for modeling semantics and pragmatic inference.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the semantics of natural language is probabilistic in nature, in that the interpretation of a natural language utterance is a probabilistic model over possible worlds.

probabilistic models of natural language meaning and use should be grounded in conceptual structure, with lexical semantics and pragmatic reasoning as the key connecting links between cognition and communication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to build a probabilistic semantics for natural language, which we call probabilistic compositional semantics.
we are developing a probabilistic theory of language meaning and interpretation that is grounded in human conceptual structure.
probabilistic models can help us to understand how we use words, how we understand sentences, and what we can infer from the words and sentences of other people.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a probabilistic model can be used to capture the full range of linguistic phenomena in a single formalism.
probabilistic models are a natural fit for describing the complex, uncertain, and context-sensitive aspects of language and cognition.
the semantics and pragmatically inferred meanings that are the basis for language understanding are grounded in a probabilistic conceptual structure.
